title: Yara and the Confession
premise: Estate lawyer Zephyrine Crane is summoned to Blackthorn House to read the will of Marguerite Vale, a woman who vanished thirty years ago and was declared dead without a body. The will shouldn't exist, and neither should the diary found with it — a diary whose entries continue for two years past the date of Marguerite's disappearance. As Zephyrine, alongside the estranged Vale heir Theo and housekeeper's daughter Imogen, decodes entries that name three 'accidents' she recognizes from her own cold-case work, they discover Marguerite faked her death to escape a family pact sealed at an anniversary dinner — and someone in the household has been killing to keep it buried. At the anniversary dinner, Zephyrine exposes the killer: the family patriarch's devoted solicitor, who has murdered twice more to protect the secret, and Marguerite herself steps out of hiding to testify, choosing love over the duty that once silenced her.
about_author: Astrid Joubert is a former probate clerk from the Channel Islands who spent a decade handling disputed estates before turning to fiction. Her mysteries are known for their legal precision and their fascination with the secrets families seal into paper.

chapters.title: The Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Zephyrine Crane arrives at rain-soaked Blackthorn House to execute a will for Marguerite Vale, missing thirty years and legally dead. The document is dated after the disappearance. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: unease masked as professional composure.

chapters.title: Heirs and Ghosts
chapters.summary: Zephyrine meets the beneficiaries: bitter grandson Theo, sharp-eyed Imogen whose mother kept the house, and patriarch Edmund Vale, frail but watchful. Each reacts strangely to Marguerite's name. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: the sense of a family performing grief.

chapters.title: Three Accidents
chapters.summary: Reviewing estate records, Zephyrine recognizes the pattern: three deaths over thirty years, all ruled accidental, all echoing cases she quietly solved before. She begins a private file. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: the thrill and dread of recognition.

chapters.title: Imogen's Keys
chapters.summary: Imogen reveals a locked writing desk Marguerite left behind; her mother always said it held 'the truth that pays the wages.' They find no key — only scratch marks inside the drawer. POV: Imogen. Emotional beat: loyalty torn between mother's silence and her own curiosity.

chapters.title: The Diary Begins
chapters.summary: Theo pries open the desk and finds Marguerite's diary, its early pages ordinary — garden parties, a sister's wedding, a growing fear of 'the dinner.' POV: Theo. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness toward a grandmother he resented.

chapters.title: Past the Last Page
chapters.summary: The diary continues two years beyond the date Marguerite vanished. Someone wrote those pages — or she never left. Zephyrine realizes the police timeline is fiction. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: vertigo as the case rewrites itself.

chapters.title: What the Dinner Toasts
chapters.summary: Edmund announces the thirtieth anniversary dinner will proceed as tradition demands, glass raised to absent Marguerite. The household stiffens. Zephyrine notes who flinches. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: dread dressed as etiquette.

chapters.title: Alibi, Thirty Years Old
chapters.summary: Zephyrine interviews the surviving staff about the night of the disappearance. Their alibis are word-for-word identical — rehearsed. Only old gardener Pell hesitates. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: patience sharpening into suspicion.

chapters.title: The Sister's Letters
chapters.summary: In the attic, Imogen finds letters between Marguerite and her late sister referencing 'the arrangement' and a sum paid annually to an unnamed recipient. POV: Imogen. Emotional beat: betrayal — the family she served was bought.

chapters.title: A Visitor in the Night
chapters.summary: Someone searches Zephyrine's room; her case file is disturbed but not taken. A warning note: 'Some wills are wishes.' POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: fear converted to defiance.

chapters.title: Pell's Silence Breaks
chapters.summary: Gardener Pell admits he saw Marguerite alive weeks after her disappearance, boarding a coastal bus — and that solicitor Mr. Halloway paid him to forget. Days later, Pell is found drowned. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: guilt for asking questions that cost a life.

chapters.title: Halloway's Perfect Record
chapters.summary: Zephyrine investigates Halloway, the family solicitor for forty years: spotless, indispensable, present at every death and every anniversary dinner. His alibis span decades like chain mail. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: admiration curdling into horror.

chapters.title: The Arrangement
chapters.summary: Decoding the diary's coded margins, they learn 'the arrangement': Edmund covered up a fatal hit-and-run by his son, paying the victim's family through Halloway — and Marguerite discovered it. POV: Imogen. Emotional beat: pity for a family rotting under one secret.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Choice
chapters.summary: Diary entries reveal Marguerite didn't flee guilt but staged her death when Halloway threatened her — duty to family versus love for a woman she could never acknowledge. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: grief reframed as understanding.

chapters.title: The Second Will
chapters.summary: Zephyrine finds the real will hidden in the diary's binding: everything to Marguerite's beloved, on condition the arrangement be exposed. Halloway has been searching for it for thirty years. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by danger.

chapters.title: Locked In
chapters.summary: Storm seals the roads; phones fail. Halloway locks the archive wing with Zephyrine inside and sets a small fire to destroy records. She escapes through the servant passages Imogen showed her. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: terror met with resourcefulness.

chapters.title: Confessions Over Brandy
chapters.summary: Edmund, dying, confesses the cover-up to Theo and begs him to end it — then dies before dawn, his medication suspiciously altered. Halloway now controls the estate's papers. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: orphaned anger finding purpose.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: Halloway insists the dinner proceed, glass raised to Marguerite, every heir assembled — the perfect room for a final tidy-up. Zephyrine accepts her seat knowing it's a trap she must spring herself. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: calm on the edge of catastrophe.

chapters.title: The Toast
chapters.summary: As glasses rise, Zephyrine reads the second will aloud and lays out the three accidents, Pell's drowning, and the rehearsed alibis. Staff turn on Halloway; he produces a pistol. POV: multiple, rapid cuts. Emotional beat: the held breath before breaking.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: Imogen disarms Halloway using the servant-passage knowledge her mother passed down; Theo shields Zephyrine. Halloway breaks, confessing he killed to protect not Edmund but the order he built. POV: Imogen. Emotional beat: courage inherited, finally honored.

chapters.title: The Woman at the Gate
chapters.summary: Police take Halloway away. At the gate stands an elderly woman with Marguerite's eyes — alive, having watched the lights of the dinner from the road. She embraces Theo and asks only whether the will was read. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: thirty years of absence collapsing into one embrace.

chapters.title: What the Glass Holds
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the estate passes to Theo and Imogen jointly; Marguerite, cleared, chooses a cottage by that coastal bus route. Zephyrine raises a private glass to the dead who were heard at last — and takes a new case file from her bag. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: peace earned, hunger for the next truth kindled.
